These findings suggest that leptin deficiency enhances insular interoception of cue-induced feelings of hunger and is associated with enhanced activation of parietal, temporal, and occipital regions.

description.value: This study examined how leptin replacement alters brain responses to high- and low-calorie food cues in three adults with congenital leptin deficiency using fMRI.

spans.text: We addressed this question by pairing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) with presentation of food images to the three leptin-deficient adults with the Arg105Trp mutation with and without leptin treatment.

value: We hypothesized that leptin replacement would alter ratings of hunger induced by the food-related stimuli and that this would occur along with changes in activation of the previously identified brain regions by the food-related cues in the congenitally leptin-deficient research participants.
